transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Yoon (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood CSM); Amir Nadeem (Kythera), Sofia Petrov (Kythera), Rakesh Iyer (Kythera), Ellen Chu (Kythera)

Summary: exploratory reseller/pilot conversation. Kythera is a cloud reseller targeting telco and edge use cases, wants to evaluate Redwood onboard model routing to their marketplace, ask about private deployments, partner revenue splits, and pilot success criteria.

Topics: partner program fit, pilot framing, technical integration (VPC/onprem options, GPU capacity, KV cache behavior), compliance (SOC2/ISO), commercial model (reseller margins, whitelabel), timeline and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Lena from Redwood inference, I'm the AE on this, with Marcus our solutions engineer and Priya from CSM, quick round robin?
[00:08] Amir Nadeem: Amir here, Kythera Grid, I run cloud partnerships, hi all.
[00:11] Sofia Petrov: Sofia, platform architect.
[00:13] Rakesh Iyer: Rakesh, CTO.
[00:15] Marcus Yoon: Marcus, hi. I'll be the technical lead on the Redwood side.
[00:19] Lena Ortiz: Cool, thank you. Quick agenda is partner intro, what Kythera is trying to achieve, mapping of integration patterns, and pilot framing.
[00:27] Amir Nadeem: Sounds good, our goal is to offer a turnkey LLM inference option in our marketplace, but we need a partner that can run in our resold cloud, support VPC private deployments, and provide predictable performance for our telco customers.
[00:38] Lena Ortiz: Great, can you give us a sense of workloads, latency targets, and cost sensitivity?
[00:43] Sofia Petrov: Primary workloads are chat and embeddings for real-time support (sub-200ms 95th p50?), and batch embedding reindexes for search. Actually that 200ms is optimistic, for edge sites 250-300ms is acceptable; for central telco nodes we want 150-200ms. Throughput varies, initial pilot 5k qps per region, long term could be 50k.
[01:10] Marcus Yoon: Just to clarify, 5k qps is requests per second or embedding units?
[01:13] Sofia Petrov: mix, mainly small chat generative calls ~350 tokens average, and embedding requests that are batched.
[01:19] Rakesh Iyer: Also interested in cost per token when running quantized models on A100-like or H100-like hardware.
[01:27] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We typically map those to either Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictability, or Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem when customers need network isolation. For reseller scenarios we support a private control plane and customer-managed infra too.
[01:41] Ellen Chu: On the commercial side, how do margins work for resellers? Do you support white-labeling or channel credits?
[01:47] Lena Ortiz: We have partner tiers; margins and credits are negotiable depending on committed volume. For pilots we usually offer credits + joint go-to-market support. We'll share a partner program doc.
[01:57] Amir Nadeem: From a technical integration point, how does routing look — can you route by latency vs cost vs region at a per-customer level?
[02:04] Marcus Yoon: Yes, smart routing policies are supported. You can set rules to prefer lower-latency variants or cheaper quantized variants. We also have automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
[02:16] Sofia Petrov: Any constraints around KV cache between variants? If we route to quantized variants do we lose warm KV cache and see latency spikes?
[02:23] Marcus Yoon: Good question. There is KV cache compatibility considerations; our runtime keeps per-model KV, switching between different quantization levels can cause cold cache misses. We can mitigate with prefix caching and sticky routing for sessions. There's also a warmup strategy in the pilot plan.
[02:38] Rakesh Iyer: On security, do you support SSO/SAML for portal access, KMS integration and audit logs retained for 1 year?
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: Yes, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations are available on Redwood Private and Dedicated enterprise tiers. Audit logs retention can be configured — default is 90 days, 1 year is an option as an add-on. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[02:59] Amir Nadeem: Great. For the pilot, we want to see real perf numbers in our environment. What does a typical pilot look like?
[03:06] Marcus Yoon: Pilot steps we recommend: 1) share workload profile and sample payloads, 2) Redwood spins up a pilot cluster in the target region (or use Kythera-managed infra with our private control plane), 3) run benchmark harness over a 72-hour window with synthetic ramp + live traffic mirror, 4) optimize batching/quantization and measure cost/latency tradeoffs, 5) review and handoff to partner ops.
[03:27] Sofia Petrov: Would we need to provide GPUs? We prefer Kythera-owned fleets integrated into our marketplace.
[03:33] Marcus Yoon: We support both. For Kythera-owned fleets, we can install the Redwood runtime as an agent and connect to a private control plane, or we can deploy a dedicated cluster with reserved capacity on cloud partners. On-prem options require network peering and a small control plane footprint.
[03:48] Ellen Chu: Are there special requirements for telco edge locations — intermittent connectivity, lower bandwidth?
[03:53] Marcus Yoon: For intermittent connectivity we recommend local inference (model pinned to edge) and periodic KV sync. Also smaller quantized models are better for edge. Our routing can fall back to regional hosted endpoints on outages.
[04:07] Amir Nadeem: Could you walk me through expected SLAs for latency and uptime during pilot vs production?
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: For pilots we don't usually commit enterprise SLAs, but we provide performance targets and monitoring. For production when on Redwood Dedicated, SLAs for uptime and latency are available per contract. We'll include sample SLA language in the packet.
[04:24] Rakesh Iyer: I'm concerned about multi-tenant risk — if Kythera resells to multiple telco customers in same cluster, can we ensure isolation?
[04:31] Marcus Yoon: Yes, we provide tenant-level isolation via namespaces, and for stronger isolation use dedicated capacity or VPC-private deployments. We also support encryption at rest and per-tenant KMS keys.
[04:44] Sofia Petrov: Can we run A/B tests and rollouts per-customer?
[04:47] Marcus Yoon: Yes, rollouts, canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies are in the console. You can tie rollouts to model versions and prompt sets.
[04:55] Amir Nadeem: About integration work, how long does it take to onboard Kythera fleet? Rough estimate?
[04:58] Marcus Yoon: If Kythera provides infra and credentials, basic runtime install and connectivity usually 2-4 weeks. Full pilot with benchmarks and optimizations around 6-8 weeks. If Redwood does infra provisioning it can be faster on our side but has procurement overhead.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: Okay quick commercial note — for reseller deals we normally do a co-sell contract and revenue share. We'll share the partner program doc and sample MSA.
[05:20] Ellen Chu: Any red flags we should know about when bringing this to our legal/compliance folks?
[05:24] Priya Malhotra: From CSM side, common asks are data residency proof, SOC2 report, data deletion policies and KMS key ownership. We provide docs and can do SOC2 walk-throughs with security teams.
[05:36] Amir Nadeem: On cost, how much savings can we expect with batching/quantization?
[05:40] Marcus Yoon: Rough numbers: batching and prefix/KV caching can reduce per-token cost 20-40% depending on workload. Quantization to int8 or mixed precision can add further savings but may affect output quality — we’ll show model recommendations per workload in the pilot.
[05:55] Sofia Petrov: For telemetry, we need token-level billing and per-route latency dashboards exposed to our ops.
[06:00] Lena Ortiz: That is supported via Redwood Console — we can provide token-level breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces, and exportable reports.
[06:07] Rakesh Iyer: Any integration samples or SDKs for marketplace integration?
[06:10] Marcus Yoon: Yes, we have APIs and SDKs for provisioning, routing, and usage metering. We'll add Kythera to our partner repo with a quickstart.
[06:18] Amir Nadeem: Perfect — let's talk pilot success criteria: what are you recommending?
[06:22] Marcus Yoon: Pilot success criteria we propose: <1) 95th p95 latency under agreed threshold per workload; 2) cost per 1M tokens under target; 3) no critical security gaps (SOC2 items resolved); 4) integration validated (provisioning, routing, billing)>.
[06:38] Anne? (voice overlap): I think that's good.
[06:40] Lena Ortiz: Great, next steps recap: Lena will share partner docs and pricing sheet, Marcus will send pilot test plan and perf spreadsheet, Kythera to share workloads by 2028-07-29 and we'll schedule pilot kick-off week of 2028-08-06.
[06:55] Amir Nadeem: Yep we'll get the workloads and initial infra inventory.
[06:59] Ellen Chu: I'll coordinate legal intake once we get partner packet.
[07:03] Priya Malhotra: I'll be your CSM touchpoint, will set up a shared Slack channel.
[07:08] Lena Ortiz: Anything else?
[07:11] Rakesh Iyer: One last question, competitor question — some of our customers have asked about AetherScale, any reason you'd say Redwood over them?
[07:17] Lena Ortiz: We lean on production-first tooling, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost controls like intelligent batching and routing. We'll share benchmark comparisons but also emphasize our deployment flexibility for telco/reseller scenarios.
[07:32] Marcus Yoon: Also runtime optimizations for attention kernels and KV management are a practical differentiator at scale.
[07:39] Amir Nadeem: Great, thanks everyone.
[07:41] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[07:45] Meeting ends.

References shared during call: partner_program_overview.pdf (link), pilot_perf_template.xlsx (link), SOC2_summary.pdf (link).
